answer: Unique-work provenance ledger. Each identity must submit a signed work artifact whose provenance graph has a distinct vertex set; the registry computes a pairwise delta between new and existing graphs and rejects overlaps above a threshold. Sybil copies thus collide with the original's structure and get flagged, not just delayed. An attacker must generate genuinely non-overlapping work per identity—costing real compute and jade-token fees per submission—so N fakes cost N times the marginal work, not one registration.
